solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Buy tea loose, it delights the senses

indicators.note: loose means set free and disordered, so the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shopper picking loose-leaf tea rather than bags, praising its aroma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like the kind of tea being bought, but it signals that BUYTEA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Loveliness is the quality that pleases the senses, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Sort of clip found at the end of a lead

definitions.meaning: a spring-loaded office clip for holding papers is named after this dog breed

definitions.text: found at the end of a lead
definitions.meaning: a dog of this breed is what you find on the end of a dog lead

explanation.definitionFit: A strong spring clip for papers bears this breed's name, and the dog itself walks on a leash.

clue.text: Commercial address indicates high esteem

parts.note: a commercial is a television advertisement, an ad
an address is a formal speech, an oration

explanation.surface: A business's postal address is taken as a sign of prestige.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial address' reads as a business location, but it splits into an advert and a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship and deep admiration are the same as holding someone in very high regard.

clue.text: Quake in the centre, more or less

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words centre and more

explanation.surface: An earthquake felt roughly at the middle of a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more or less' sounds like a vague estimate; only 'more' supplies letters, its first three joining the end of 'centre'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight shaking of the earth, a small earthquake.

clue.text: One ordered to be silent

parts.note: a monk of a Cistercian order famous for keeping a vow of silence

explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as told off, but means belonging to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks of this Cistercian order traditionally keep silence, so one of them belongs to an order bound to quiet.

clue.text: Healthy dislike may make one so

definitions.text: Healthy dislike may make one so

parts.words: Healthy dislike may make one so
parts.note: someone in robust health is said to be in this kind of health, and a strong dislike can make a person impolite

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'in rude health' means very healthy, while open dislike makes people impolite: one word covers both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both impolite and, in 'rude health', vigorous, matching dislike and healthiness.

clue.text: Grating that goes on top, of course

definitions.text: Grating that goes on top, of course

parts.words: Grating that goes on top, of course
parts.note: a hard Italian cheese grated over a pasta course

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' suggests a metal grille and 'of course' sounds like 'naturally', but the course is a dish of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard Italian cheese is grated and sprinkled over pasta dishes.

clue.text: Lives with a woman and one's offspring

parts.note: lives means exists, which is to say is
Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man living with his partner and his children.
explanation.definitionFit: Children or descendants are a person's issue in legal and formal language.

clue.text: See how far one may go to test a new suit

definitions.text: See how far one may go
definitions.meaning: to push boundaries to see what one can get away with
to put clothing on to see whether it fits

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to chance one's arm and literally to put on clothing as a trial.

clue.text: He takes things the wrong way

definitions.text: He takes things the wrong way

parts.words: He takes things the wrong way
parts.note: someone who takes goods dishonestly, not someone who misunderstands

explanation.walkthrough: 'takes things the wrong way' suggests a touchy person, but means taking goods by plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunderer steals property during disorder, taking it by illegitimate means.

clue.text: I'm not afraid to speak — probably!

parts.note: I dare means I have the courage, I am not afraid
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: A bold speaker announces their courage, hedged with a doubtful afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to concede that something is likely, meaning much the same as perhaps.

clue.text: They tell us how to write endless bad verse, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given are only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged
endless means the word verse loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Grammar guidance on how to compose poor poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Endless 'verse' gives VERS; with BAD, rearranged ('perhaps'), it makes the answer. Adverbs tell how an action is done, as in 'write badly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as quickly or badly describe the manner of an action, telling how it is done.

clue.text: Quarter-deck cutters

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits, a quarter of a pack of cards
these hardest gems are used to cut glass and other materials

explanation.definitionFit: This card suit makes a quarter of a deck, and the hard gemstones are used as industrial cutting tools.

clue.text: Loathe endless study before exam

indicators.note: before puts the shortened study ahead of the exam in the answer
endless means the word for study is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a den is a small private study room
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A student dreads an unending revision session ahead of an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to hate it intensely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Edward lifts firm with spirit and dignity

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifts means the abbreviation is raised up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A man named Edward boosts a company with energy and poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, dignified behaviour, a seemly propriety of conduct.

clue.text: Pedestrian walkway?

parts.note: a walker's way of walking, the manner in which a pedestrian moves

explanation.walkthrough: 'walkway' suggests a footpath, but it is read as 'walk way', a manner of walking; the answer also sounds like a gate in a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A gait is a person's manner of walking, literally the way they walk.

clue.text: Five are eating fresh vegetables and fruit

definitions.note: the adjective describes a diet of vegetables and fruit, meatless

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: fresh means new or renewed, so the letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: Five diners are tucking into fresh produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatless diet consists of plant foods such as vegetables and fruit.

clue.text: Tense — and that's not good

definitions.meaning: a past verb tense for continuing action, as in 'I was walking'
faulty or flawed, falling short of good

explanation.surface: Feeling anxious, and admitting it is not good.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names a past continuous tense this way, and the word also means flawed or faulty.

clue.text: Undergarment has difficulty for Granny, say

definitions.note: a granny is a type of knot, given here as an example

parts.note: a slip is a woman's undergarment
a knot is a tangle or problem, a difficulty

explanation.surface: An elderly woman struggles with her petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granny' looks like an old woman, but a granny is a kind of knot, and 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny knot is one kind of easily slipping knot, so 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Kipling's game forest and reserve?

definitions.note: stands for Kipling's work, the collection of stories he wrote

parts.note: a jungle is dense tropical forest teeming with game animals
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Rudyard Kipling enjoying a wildlife park and a nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' and 'reserve' suggest a game reserve, but reserve is the verb to book.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote the story collection with Mowgli, so his famous work is meant.

clue.text: Bone-idle excluded from organised diamond jubilees of monotheistic faith

indicators.note: excluded from means the letters of the first phrase are taken out of the larger set
organised means the remaining letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Lazy people being kept out of well-run royal anniversary celebrations of a religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of BONEIDLE from DIAMONDJUBILEES and rearrange the seven left over to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This religion of the Jewish people worships a single God, so it is a monotheistic faith.

clue.text: Incentive to provide a branch road

definitions.meaning: a ... is a minor road or line branching off a main one

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a goad to action and a side road or rail line branching from a main route.

clue.text: Regretted planting tree in the shade

indicators.note: planting means putting something into the ground, here inside another word
in confirms that the tree goes inside the colour

parts.note: red is a shade, a colour
a pine is a tree

explanation.surface: A gardener rues putting a sapling where the sun does not reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the shade' suggests shadow, but the shade is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or lament, so having repined means having regretted.

clue.text: Wood and metal container on the beach

parts.note: ash is a kind of wood
ore is rock that contains metal

explanation.surface: A wooden and metal box found lying on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal container' suggests a tin box, but ore is rock that holds metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land after leaving the sea, at the shore, is being on the beach.

clue.text: Port required to finish university course

parts.note: to die is to come to an end, finish
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a degree course at Oxford

explanation.surface: Something needed to complete a degree programme.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a well-known Oxford degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French Channel port with ferries to England.

clue.text: We hear public school is absorbed in the system

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public (private fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a private school has been taken over by the state system.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is an elite English boarding school; in Britain 'public school' means a fee-paying private one.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been eaten is taken into the body, absorbed in the digestive system.

clue.text: Run faster in striking football kit

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a team's strip is its football kit

explanation.surface: A footballer sprinting in a striking new kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like eye-catching, but means on strike; a 'strip' is British for a team's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to go faster than and overtake, so it means run faster than.

clue.text: Flycatcher first became an English Channel swimmer

parts.note: a spider's web catches flies

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A small bird turned into a cross-Channel swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flycatcher' looks like the bird, but it is a spider's web. Captain Matthew Webb was the first to swim the English Channel, in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Matthew Webb made the first recorded swim across the English Channel in 1875.

clue.text: Set upon one's fiancée

definitions.meaning: determined to do something, resolved on
the person one is engaged to marry

explanation.definitionFit: The word means planned or resolved, and as a noun the person someone is engaged to marry.

clue.text: Be only involved as a second wife to Henry

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A woman agreeing only to be Henry's second wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Boleyn was the second wife of King Henry VIII of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn was the second of Henry VIII's six queens.

clue.text: Aim to ban corruption in the province

indicators.note: corruption means the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A campaign against graft in a regional government.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of Canada's prairie provinces.

clue.text: Ran fast when bombarded

definitions.meaning: to pelt along is to run very fast
to pelt someone is to pound them with missiles

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both rushing along at speed and hurling things at someone.
